title: Prefill -> Decode kernel migration exposes non-atomic attention-state snapshot causing stale embedding reads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After introducing opportunistic kernel migration to a faster fused-attention implementation, we observed sporadic token duplication and small probability numerical drift in logits for long-context prefill flows. This ticket captures the investigation and remediation plan for a correctness issue where attention state snapshots become inconsistent across a kernel switch during in-flight prefill->decode transitions.
symptoms: Intermittent duplicated tokens in outputs for multi-chunk prefill scenarios (1 in ~50k requests in canary)
Small but reproducible L2-norm drift in final logits compared to baseline for identical inputs when kernel migration triggers mid-prefill
Mismatch in KV slot epoch tags observed in debug traces after a kernel handoff
Increased tail latency for affected requests due to downstream retry logic in some callers
steps_to_reproduce: Run a prefill of ~2048 tokens split into 8 chunks with concurrent decode enabled (batching factor 4)
Force kernel migration by enabling 'candidate_score_boost' and reduce cooldown so handoff is likely during chunk boundary
Capture debug KV traces (KV_EPOCH and KV_SLOT checksums) and full logits for each token position
Compare outputs to a baseline run without kernel migration and note any token duplication or per-step logit divergence
logs: 2026-02-20T12:03:14Z WARN kernel_migrator: handoff initiated for shard-3 while prefill chunk 5 inflight
2026-02-20T12:03:14Z ERROR decoder: token_duplication detected at output_pos=631 request_id=rx-94b2
investigation_summary: Initial triage shows the migrator performs a host-side swap of the shard's KV base pointer and immediately schedules the new kernel without ensuring all in-flight decoders have observed a consistent snapshot. On some GPUs this exposes a memory ordering gap: the kernel reads a KV slot before the host pointer update is fully visible or before the migrating kernel has completed zeroing/initialization of new cache metadata. The result is a stale epoch read followed by writes that produce token duplication and slight logit drift. Reproduced locally with debug builds and a synthetic harness that interleaves prefill chunk boundaries with an explicit 'migrate' signal.
root_cause: Non-atomic handoff path in the kernel migrator: host-side pointer swap + immediate kernel launch lacks a strict synchronization/fence guaranteeing visibility of initialized KV metadata to the newly launched kernel. Additionally, the KV metadata lacked a monotonically-incrementing slot epoch tag that would let kernels detect stale reads and self-heal.
proposed_mitigation: Short-term: add a conservative quiesce step where the migrator waits for in-flight prefill decoders to reach a safe boundary before switching pointers (configurable via 'migrator_quiesce_ms', default 2ms)

Medium-term: make the pointer swap atomic from the kernel's perspective by using CUDA atomic compare-and-swap on a single migration descriptor and issuing CUDAStream.synchronize or cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirect (platform-specific) to enforce visibility
Long-term: embed per-slot monotonically-incrementing epoch tags and checksum validation; new kernels must verify slot epoch >= expected and fall back to reinitialization on mismatch
Add a runtime flag 'disable_optimistic_migration' for controlled rollbacks in canary
mitigation_risks: Quiesce increases latency slightly for migration cases and could reduce throughput under heavy churn. Atomic CUDA operations add overhead for each migration but are rare; epoch tags increase KV metadata size by 8 bytes per slot.
tests_added: Microbenchmark harness that fuzzes migration timing against prefill chunk boundaries and asserts no token duplication across 1M synthetic traces
Unit test for kv_manager that simulates concurrent read/write with epoch tags and verifies detection and recovery paths
Integration canary that enables migration on 1% of traffic with enhanced logging and automatic rollback on error rate > 0.1%
acceptance_criteria: No token duplication observed under the microbenchmark across 1M runs
Canary traffic (1%) shows error rate <= baseline + 0.05% for 72h
KV post-swap validation logs no epoch mismatches in production canary
Performance regression < 0.5% p50 and < 2% p99 compared to pre-change baseline when migration is idle
